# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`); uv workspace, code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (spec §4.9).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes downloaded for a chosen range of quarters, as the baseline | R1; §2.1 Backfill; §4.2 Backfill | A | 1 | Depends on `backfill.start_quarter` (unset). Bytes per quarterly file are measured by Stage 1. At most 136 quarters (1993–2026), so one request per file at 3 req/s is under a minute of SEC traffic |
| O2 | New daily filing indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, including catch-up after missed runs | R2; §4.2 Daily ingestion | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year, plus listing requests; negligible at 3 req/s |
| O3 | A clean, deduplicated filing-index table in Parquet built from those indexes | R3; §4.5 row contract; §4.6 | A | 3 | Measured by Stage 1 (elapsed time, peak memory per quarter) |
| O4 | The pipeline running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Azure Monitor | R4; §4.1; §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend unknown until it runs; measured by Stage 7's smoke test |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | none material |
| O6 | Original index files kept, so a parser change reprocesses them without downloading again | R6; §4.3 validation; §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage roughly equal to the total raw bytes from O1 and O2 |
| O7 | Past quarters re-checked on a schedule, with their corrections applied | R7; §4.2 Reconciliation; §4.4 | A | 7 | One request per supported quarter per weekly run; at most 136 requests, about 45 s at 3 req/s |
| O8 | All SEC traffic under one request budget, however many workers run | R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | none material |
| O9 | Readers always see a complete, versioned dataset through one active pointer per quarter | R9; §4.5; §4.6 Publish | A | 9 | none material |
| O10 | Records leave the active catalog only after explicit approval, tied to the source hash, for a closed quarter | R10; §4.4 Closed quarter | A | 10 | Operator time per gated candidate |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and the rate target set as reviewed starting values | R11; §4.8 | A | 11 | none material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Single-quarter index to Parquet (core)
      Objective: Fetch one real archived quarterly master index from the SEC and turn it into canonical filing-index rows in local Parquet.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: the generated `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` scaffold only
      Produces: a `sec-edgar-ingest` command that fetches one named quarter with an identifying User-Agent at no more than 3 req/s and writes `sec-index-v1` rows; golden fixtures for that quarter's format; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one closed quarter's master.idx is fetched from the SEC, and each data row is either parsed or refused with its line and reason. O3 — the Parquet row count matches the parsed rows, and the fields meet the §4.5 row contract. The findings file records the measured cost of the real run: bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and SEC request count.
      Leaves out: raw snapshots and replay → Stage 2; source manifest and checkpoints → Stage 3; shared request lease → Stage 4; versioned manifests and active pointer → Stage 5; Azure deployment, observability and alerts → Stage 7; scheduling, trigger enablement and runbooks → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Raw snapshots and replay
      Objective: Keep every download as validated, content-addressed original bytes, and rebuild observations from them without contacting the SEC.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's fetch command, parser and row contract
      Produces: raw snapshots and replay: raw, quarantine and observation stores at the §4.5 paths on a local backend, keyed by hash, parser version and schema version; a replay command that makes no SEC requests
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version bump rebuilds Stage 1's quarter from raw storage with zero SEC requests and identical logical rows. An HTML or truncated body is quarantined and never parsed as an empty index (§6 Replay, Parsing).
      Leaves out: source manifest and checkpoints → Stage 3; ADLS as the store (Azure deployment) → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Backfill range and daily catch-up
      Objective: Run one shared discover → collect → transform path over a configured quarter range and over daily indexes, checkpointed per source file.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 2's raw store and replay command
      Produces: source manifest and checkpoints: the `discover`, `collect` and `transform` commands; immutable worksets; source, snapshot, workset-binding, processing and attempt records (§4.5) on a local backend; deduplication of the baseline/daily overlap; golden fixtures for every format in the chosen range
      Exit: O1 — a configured range runs and reports complete, pending and failed units separately. O2 — daily discovery from `daily.start_date` catches up across a quarter boundary, reports `no_new_sources` on a valid empty listing, and does not advance past a failed listing. O5 — backfill and daily runs call the same downloader, parser and transform code (§6 Discovery and coverage).
      Leaves out: shared request lease → Stage 4; versioned manifests and active pointer → Stage 5; Table Storage backend (Azure deployment) → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: One SEC request budget
      Objective: Route all SEC traffic through one leased collector with bounded retries.
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stage 3's discover and collect commands
      Produces: shared request lease: Storage-backed lease coordination; retry, backoff and Retry-After handling; halt on access denial; validation of the §4.8 `sec.*` and `http.*` keys before any I/O
      Exit: O8 — concurrent backfill and daily collectors never overlap as request issuers, retries count toward the budget, a lost lease stops requests, and a 403 halts the run (§6 Access).
      Leaves out: deployed Storage account (Azure deployment) → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each affected quarter as a complete generation behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3's processing records and observation output
      Produces: versioned manifests and active pointer: the `publish` command; per-quarter generations with `manifest.json` and `changes.parquet`; the conditional pointer; the reader contract (§4.6 Publish)
      Exit: O9 — crashes injected at all three points leave readers seeing only complete generations, competing publishers lose no update, and a repeated publish creates no duplicate logical records (§6 Publication).
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate → Stage 6; Table Storage pointer (Azure deployment) → Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes, apply safe changes, and gate key removals behind approval tied to the source hash.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stage 4's request budget; Stage 5's publication path
      Produces: withdrawal gate: reconciliation source selection; open- and closed-quarter precedence (§4.4); `awaiting_approval` candidates and approval records
      Exit: O7 — unchanged hashes skip work, and additions and field updates publish with change records. O10 — a closed-quarter candidate that removes keys stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval names its source hash; open-quarter absence and HTTP failures withdraw nothing; a stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key (§6 Reconciliation).
      Leaves out: approval runbook (runbooks) → Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure platform
      Objective: Run the shared image on Azure with orchestration, storage, identities and monitoring, with all triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: the ADR and spec accepted (§7 step 1); the commands and local backends from Stages 2–6
      Produces: Azure deployment, observability and alerts: one image; ADLS and Table Storage backends; the lease on a deployed Storage account; ADF pipelines that start and poll Container Apps Jobs; managed identities; logs, metrics and alerts; infrastructure under version control
      Exit: O4 — §6 Orchestration and Observability tests pass; integration tests pass on isolated Azure resources; §7 steps 3–5 are recorded (live smoke test of one archived quarter and one daily index with bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest and request rate, then replay from raw storage with SEC access disabled).
      Leaves out: scheduling, trigger enablement and runbooks → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the baseline, catch daily ingestion up, and enable the schedules under a reviewed configuration.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 7's deployment
      Produces: scheduling, trigger enablement and runbooks: a reviewed configuration revision with the §4.8 starting values; the §8 runbooks; a release record
      Exit: O11 — §7 steps 6–9 are recorded: backfill results per source, with no silent gaps; the daily trigger enabled after catch-up is accepted; one manual reconciliation, then the weekly trigger; scheduled runs observed and checked against reports. The release record names the image and configuration versions and the active generations.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Every numbered spec requirement (R1–R11) is cited by an outcome's Spec cell. Unmet outcomes leave either as a new stage or as a recorded deferral with its reason.
